situation: Coworker Raj asked me to take his on-call shift the weekend of Oct 17. I've already covered for him twice this quarter and that's my son's football tournament. Elena said last week she wants extra on-call hours.
reply: I can see you need the weekend of the 17th covered. I can't take it this time, it's my son's football tournament. Elena said last week she wants extra on-call hours, so she might be worth asking.
note: The referral is only there because it is real; skip it if you don't have one.

situation: 表哥找我借5万说要做生意，之前借的2万到现在也没还，那之后我就定了规矩，不再借钱给亲戚。不想借，但愿意帮他算算生意的账，他是我舅舅的儿子，不好撕破脸。
reply: 哥，你开口我知道不容易。这次我不借，我给自己定了规矩，亲戚之间不借钱，对谁都一样。你要是想找人一起把生意的账算一算，我可以陪你看看。
note: 用"规矩"而不是"没钱"，对方就没法在理由上讨价还价；之前那两万另找时间说，别混在这条里。

situation: A former client, Greg, asked me (graphic designer) to 'quickly' tweak his logo for free. I said no, and he's replied 'wow, after all the business I sent your way'. The tweak is about an hour's work and my rate is $90 an hour.
reply: I understand you're disappointed, Greg, and I do appreciate the referrals. My answer's the same. If you'd like to book the tweaks, it's a one-hour job at $90 and I can fit it in this week.
note: After a guilt-trip, don't re-explain. State it once, keep the paid option, then stop replying on that thread.

situation: My mother-in-law, Carol, asked if we'll host Christmas again this year, 14 people. We've done it three years running and I'm worn out. Want to say no by text but still contribute something.
reply: Hi Carol, thanks for thinking of us. We're going to pass on hosting Christmas this year; after three years in a row we'd love a turn as guests. We're happy to bring the ham and the desserts wherever it ends up, and I can come early on the 24th to help set up. Love to you.
note: A real smaller yes, the food and the setup, keeps the no generous. Don't nominate another host; that's her call.

situation: An ex-colleague, Josh, asked me to be a reference for a job at Hollowmere Analytics; his final interview is Thursday. We only worked together on one project, a rollout Priya managed, and honestly I wasn't impressed with his work. I want to say no without trashing him.
reply: Hi Josh, thanks for thinking of me, and congrats on getting to the final round at Hollowmere. I'm going to say no to being a reference this time. We only worked together on the one project, so I couldn't give them the detail a strong reference needs. Priya, who managed you on the rollout, would do you far more good. Good luck on Thursday.
note: Declining a reference: give the true reason that doesn't judge the work, and point to someone better placed.

situation: Denise, the PTA chair at my kids' school, asked me to be treasurer this year. I've run the bake sale for 3 years, but I'm back at work full time now and I don't want a role with weekly hours. I'd still run the bake sale on Saturday 7 November.
reply: Thanks for thinking of me, Denise, I can see the treasurer spot needs filling. I'm going to say no to that one; with a full-time job this year I can't take on a role with weekly hours. I can still run the bake sale table on Saturday 7 November, if that helps.
note: A true reason that isn't up for debate, and a smaller yes that's real. Skip the offer if you don't actually want the bake sale either.

situation: 市场部的周经理在公司四十多人的大群里@我，让我这周末把他们双十一活动的海报赶出来。我是品牌组的设计，这周排期已经满了，下周一倒是能排进来；按公司流程，这类需求本来要走设计需求单。
reply: 周经理，收到，看得出双十一这边时间很紧。这周末的海报我接不了，本周的排期已经排满了。下周一我可以排进来，您这边提一张设计需求单，我周一上午第一个看。
note: 在大群里被当众@：回得简短、不带情绪，不在群里讲道理；更小的yes是真实的档期，并指向公司自己的流程，细节再私聊。

situation: My friend Jordan asked me to be the guarantor on his new apartment lease, $2,400 a month. I love him, but I don't co-sign anything for anyone. He's texting me and the lease signing is Friday. I'm free tonight and happy to help him look at other options.
reply: I can tell how much you want this place, and I'm glad you asked me straight. I'm going to say no to being your guarantor. I don't co-sign leases or loans for anyone, family included; it's a rule I keep so money never sits between me and people I care about. If it helps, I'm free tonight to help you ask the landlord whether a larger deposit could replace a guarantor before Friday.
note: A rule, not a comment on his finances, leaves nothing to argue with. Only offer the help tonight if you actually mean to give it.

situation: Someone I don't know in my neighbourhood WhatsApp group messaged me privately asking me to fill in a 20-minute survey for her master's dissertation. I don't want to, and I don't think I owe a stranger a reason.
reply: Thanks for asking, but it's not something I can help with. Good luck with the dissertation.
note: Low stakes with a near-stranger: a short, friendly no with no reason; an explanation only invites a follow-up.

situation: 对门邻居刘先生，平时就电梯里点个头，今天敲门问我国庆10月1号到7号能不能帮他们照看家里的两只猫，每天上门喂一次、铲屎。我国庆在家，但我一向不帮别人照看宠物，万一出事说不清。小区门口的喵星球宠物店有上门喂养服务。
reply: 刘先生您好，谢谢您信得过我。照猫这件事我就不接了，别人家的宠物我一向不帮忙照看，怕万一有情况担不起。小区门口的'喵星球'宠物店有上门喂养服务，您可以去问问。国庆愉快！
note: 不太熟的邻居：用一条规矩拒绝，不用编理由；有真实可用的去处就给一个，简短收尾。

situation: Mi cuñado Andrés me pidió prestado el coche una semana, del 10 al 17 de octubre, para irse a la costa con unos amigos. No presto el coche a nadie y el seguro solo me cubre a mí. El verano pasado alquilé uno en una agencia con buen precio por semana.
reply: Andrés, gracias por preguntarme directamente. Te voy a decir que no: el coche no lo presto, es una regla que tengo con todo el mundo, y además el seguro solo me cubre a mí. Si te sirve, te paso el contacto de la agencia donde alquilé el verano pasado, tenían buen precio por semana. ¡Que lo paséis genial en la costa!
note: Una regla para todos es difícil de discutir; la alternativa es pequeña y real. Si insiste: 'Te entiendo, pero mi respuesta es la misma'.

situation: My friend Ben asked me to help him move out of his third-floor walk-up on Saturday October 10. I don't want to spend the day carrying boxes, but I'm free that evening and would genuinely like to help in some other way.
reply: Thanks for asking me, Ben, and congrats on the new place. I'm going to say no to the carrying on Saturday. I can come over that evening with pizza and help build the bed and unpack the kitchen, if that's useful.
note: No reason owed for the no; the evening help is the smaller yes, and it's only there because you actually want to give it.

situation: 表姨让我帮她儿子在我们公司内推，还想让我跟HR打个招呼“关照一下”。表弟专业不太对口，公司招人的事我一向不插手，但也不想让表姨觉得我不帮忙。
reply: 表姨，我知道您是为表弟着急。跟HR打招呼这件事我不能做，公司招人我一向不插手，对谁都一样。表弟要是想试试，我把官网上正在招的岗位链接发给他，他自己投简历就行，投之前我可以帮他看一眼简历。
note: 拒绝的是“打招呼”，用一条对谁都一样的规矩；发链接和看简历是真能给的小帮助，不想做就别提。

situation: 同组同事小周让我明天早上帮他在钉钉上代打卡，他要送孩子去医院复查，大概晚到一个小时。我理解他，但考勤的事我一向不替人做。
reply: 小周，孩子复查肯定得去，我明白。代打卡这个我不帮，考勤的事我一向不碰，对谁都一样。你按公司的请假流程在钉钉上提个假，说明一下原因就行。上午群里有急事，我先帮你盯着，有情况给你打电话。
note: 拒绝的是代打卡，不是这个人：一条对谁都一样的规矩，指一条正当的路，再给一个真能做到的小帮忙。

situation: My friend Marco just opened a taco place and asked me and my partner to post 5-star online reviews this week. We haven't eaten there yet and I only review places I've been to. My partner Sam and I are planning to go on Friday night.
reply: Congrats on the opening, Marco, I know how much went into it. I'm going to say no to posting a review before we've eaten there; I only review places I've actually been to. Sam and I are coming in on Friday night though, and I'll happily write an honest review after.
note: Decline the dishonest part, not the friend; the Friday visit is the smaller yes, and only if you'll really go.

situation: 大学同学老吴找我借身份证，说他名下的手机号办满了，想用我的身份证再办一张卡，给他店里的收款账号用。我们关系不错，但证件我一向不外借。
reply: 老吴，我明白你店里收款要用。身份证我就不借了，证件这类东西我一向不外借，对谁都一样。收款的事，你可以去银行问问，看用店的名义能怎么办。
note: 用证件办卡、开账户，出了问题可能要证件主人担责，具体规定可以去营业厅或银行问清楚；拒绝时讲规矩，不评判他。

situation: 女儿明年3月产假结束，想让我从那时起每周一到周五全天帮她带孩子。我今年刚退休，想留点时间给自己，不想全天都带，但每周三可以全天去带，平时有急事也愿意搭把手。
reply: 闺女，妈知道产假结束后孩子怎么带，你心里发愁。每周五天全天带，妈就不接了，我刚退休，想给自己留点时间，这个我想好了。每周三我可以全天过来带，平时有急事也随时叫我。其他几天怎么安排，你们商量商量，需要我出主意就说。
note: 长辈拒绝子女也可以说得很清楚：一个真实理由，不道歉个没完；每周三和应急是真能给的小帮忙。

situation: 大学同学阿琳11月要来上海面试，问能不能在我家住一个星期。我一个人住一居室，一向不留人过夜，不想破例；但愿意帮她找我家附近的酒店，面试结束后请她吃顿饭。
reply: 阿琳，恭喜拿到面试！住我家这个我就不答应了，我家一向不留人过夜，对谁都一样。我可以帮你挑几家我家附近交通方便的酒店，面试结束那天我请你吃顿好的，给你庆祝一下。
note: 一条对谁都一样的规矩，比解释“家里小、不方便”更难被讨价还价；找酒店和请吃饭是真能给的小帮忙。

situation: A colleague I barely know, Ethan from sales, DMed me on Slack asking me to sponsor his charity half marathon for a children's hospital, suggesting $100. I give to a fixed set of three charities every year and don't add others, but I'm happy to share his fundraising page on LinkedIn.
reply: Hi Ethan, great cause, and good luck with the half marathon. I'm going to say no to sponsoring; I give to a fixed set of charities each year and keep it to those. I'm happy to share your fundraising page on LinkedIn today if that helps it reach more people.
note: A rule about your own giving, not a judgement on his cause, leaves nothing to negotiate; the share is the real smaller yes.

situation: My great-aunt Ruth, 84, asked me on the phone yesterday to be the executor of her will. I'm honoured, but I live in Singapore and she's in Ohio, so I couldn't be there to handle things properly. She sees her lawyer about the will next month, and I'd genuinely like to help her think through who else could do it.
reply: Aunt Ruth, I've been thinking about what you asked me yesterday, and I'm so touched you'd trust me with it. I'm going to say no to being your executor. Living in Singapore, I couldn't be there to look after things the way you deserve. I'd really like to help you think through who else could do it before you see your lawyer next month; could I call you on Sunday to talk it over? Thank you for asking me, it means a lot.
note: A big-responsibility ask: one true, practical reason and a real smaller yes; she chooses the executor, you only help her think.

situation: Jen, another mum from school, asked if I can drive her son Leo to school every Tuesday and Thursday from October. I don't drive other people's kids, as a rule for everyone. We live on the same street, so on Tuesdays I could walk Leo in with my son, Sam.
reply: Thanks for asking me, Jen, I know the school run is a juggle. I'm going to say no to driving Leo; I don't drive other people's kids, and that's the same for everyone. On Tuesdays I could walk him in with Sam, since we're on the same street, if that would help.
note: The rule does the work; the Tuesday walk is a real smaller yes, so it goes in.

situation: 高中同学阿芳现在做保险代理，这周在微信上约我聊，想让我给女儿买一份年缴8000元的重疾险。我家的保险都是我和老公一起定的，今年已经配好了，不想再加，也不想伤了同学情分。
reply: 阿芳，谢谢你想着我们家。这份保险我就不考虑了，我家的保险都是我和老公一起商量定的，今年已经配齐，不会再加了。你做这行挺不容易的，祝你顺利！有空约个饭，只聊天不聊保险哈。
note: 给一个家里的固定做法当理由，比解释预算更难被继续推销；她再约就重复同一句话。

situation: My friend Matt texted asking me to say he was at my place on Saturday night if his wife Sophie asks. He wasn't, and he won't tell me where he was. I'm not lying to Sophie for anyone, but I don't want to lecture him.
reply: I hear you, Matt, you want me to back you up about Saturday. I'm not going to do that; I don't cover for anyone, so if Sophie asks, I'll tell her to talk to you. If you want to talk about whatever's going on, I'm around.
note: No lecture and no guessing where he was; if he pushes, 'my answer's the same' and stop.

situation: Minha vizinha, dona Lurdes, tem 79 anos e mora sozinha no apartamento ao lado. Ela me pediu para guardar a senha do cartão dela e fazer os saques do mês por ela, porque tem medo de ir ao caixa eletrônico. Não quero ficar com a senha de ninguém, mas posso acompanhá-la até a agência na quinta de manhã para ela ver com o gerente outras opções.
reply: Dona Lurdes, obrigada por confiar em mim, sei que ir ao caixa eletrônico anda difícil para a senhora. Guardar a sua senha eu não vou: senha de cartão eu não guardo de ninguém, é uma regra minha com todo mundo. Mas na quinta de manhã posso ir com a senhora até a agência, para ver com o gerente que outras opções existem. É só me avisar.
note: A regra protege as duas: a senha fica só com ela. A ida à agência é o sim menor, e só entra porque é real.

situation: 小区业主群里的王阿姨私信我，让我在要求更换物业公司的联名信上签字，说已经有60多户签了。我对现在的物业还算满意，不想签。平时跟王阿姨关系不错，在电梯里经常聊天。
reply: 王阿姨，谢谢您特意来问我，这事您张罗得挺辛苦的。联名信我就不签了，我对现在的物业还算满意，不打算参与换物业的事。咱们平时该怎么聊还怎么聊，您别往心里去哈。
note: 一句真实理由就够，不评价联名对错，也不跟她争物业好坏；她再劝，就说“我的想法还是一样”。

situation: My friend Callum is going travelling for six months from November and asked if he can store his sofa, bed and about 20 boxes in my garage while he's away. We're turning the garage into a home office in January, so the space won't be free. I'd genuinely be happy to help him load the van on moving day.
reply: Thanks for asking, Callum, six months away sounds brilliant. I can't take your things in the garage; we're turning it into a home office in January, so the space won't be free. I'm happy to help you load the van on moving day though, just tell me the date.
note: A true, concrete reason with a date isn't up for debate; the van is the real smaller yes.

situation: A stranger on LinkedIn, Tobias, who's switching careers into software, asked me, a senior backend engineer, to do weekly mock interviews with him for the next two months. I don't do ongoing mentoring with people I haven't worked with, but I'm happy to give written comments on his CV once if he sends it by Friday Oct 9.
reply: Hi Tobias, thanks for reaching out, and good luck with the switch into engineering. I'm going to say no to the weekly mock interviews; I don't take on ongoing mentoring with people I haven't worked with. If it helps, send me your CV by Friday 9 October and I'll give you written comments once. Best of luck with the search.
note: A stranger asking for regular time: a rule instead of a calendar excuse, and a one-off smaller yes with a clear edge.

situation: My neighbour Graham is having an extension built and asked if his builders can come through my back garden every weekday for six weeks from 2 November, because it's easier than carrying everything through his house. I don't want people crossing my garden every day, but I'm fine with them bringing the big steel beam through once, as long as he tells me the day before.
reply: Hi Graham, thanks for asking, and good luck with the extension. I'm going to say no to daily access through the garden for the six weeks. If it helps, I'm happy for them to bring the steel beam through once, as long as you let me know the day before. Just tell me which day you're thinking.
note: Offer only the smaller yes you can live with, with its condition; before anyone crosses, check what your home insurance says about damage.

situation: 大学室友阿杰12月12日结婚，请我当婚礼司仪。我一上台讲话就紧张得发抖，不想当；但那天早上可以去帮忙接亲，也可以负责礼金登记。
reply: 阿杰，恭喜恭喜！你能想到让我当司仪，我挺感动的。司仪这个我就不接了，我一上台讲话就紧张得发抖，怕耽误你的大日子。那天早上接亲我一定到，礼金登记也交给我，你放心。
note: 拒绝的是司仪这个角色，不是婚礼本身；理由真实一句就够，接亲和礼金登记是真能给的帮忙。

situation: My manager, Graham, asked if I could spend a couple of Saturdays helping his daughter Ellie with her university personal statement, since I studied English. I keep my weekends for myself and don't want to start doing personal favours for my boss. I'd be happy to send Ellie the guide I used when I applied.
reply: Thanks for thinking of me, Graham, I can tell you want Ellie's statement to be as strong as it can be. I'm going to say no to the Saturdays; I keep my weekends for myself. I'm happy to send Ellie the guide I used when I applied, if that would help. I hope it goes really well for her.
note: A personal favour from a boss gets the same short no as anyone's: one true reason, no apology spiral, and the smaller yes only because it's real.

situation: My cousin Hannah asked me to be godmother to her baby son, Rory, at his christening on Sunday 8 November. I'm not religious and wouldn't feel right making the promises in church, but I'd love to be at the christening and be a really involved part of Rory's life.
reply: Hannah, I'm so touched you asked me, and I love that you want me in Rory's life. I'm going to say no to being his godmother; I'm not religious, and I wouldn't feel right making those promises in church. I'll absolutely be there on Sunday 8 November, and I'd love to be a really involved part of Rory's life as he grows up. Thank you for asking, it means a lot.
note: Decline the role, not the child: a true reason about yourself, no comment on their faith, and only the smaller yes you mean.

situation: I work at Northgate Appliances, and my friend Dom asked if I'd buy a £900 fridge for him with my 30% staff discount. Staff policy says the discount is only for staff and immediate family. Our store-wide sale starts on Monday 12 October and is open to everyone.
reply: I get it, Dom, £900 is a lot for a fridge. I can't use my staff discount for you; it's only for staff and immediate family, and I stick to that. Our store-wide sale starts on Monday 12 October and it's open to everyone, so it might be worth waiting for. Happy fridge hunting!
note: The employer's rule is the one reason, so there's nothing to negotiate; the sale date is a real smaller yes that doesn't bend it.
